clips.title: HashiCorp Packer Tutorial: Building Custom Images for AWS, Azure, and Docker
clips.why: The problem with setting up each machine after it starts: machines drift apart and setup takes time on every one. That is why we bake.
look: Why configuring machines one by one makes them differ over time.
How much time setup costs when it is repeated on every machine.
The idea that leads to images: do the work once, start every machine from the result.
clips.after: Our nightly image is that result: the slow setup is baked once, and each run only freshens the difference.

clips.title: Artifact Promotion - Stop Rebuilding in CI/CD
clips.why: Build once, test that exact artifact, then promote it: the rule our nightly image follows.
look: Why rebuilding for each environment lets differences creep in.
Build once, and move the same artifact forward only after it passed.
Settings that differ per environment stay outside the artifact.
clips.after: The smoke test runs on the exact image that is promoted, and per-run settings such as the capability are written at claim time, never baked.

practice.q: Complete the line in freshen that hashes the run's lockfile.
practice.hint: The command that prints a SHA-256 fingerprint of a file.
practice.why: The same tool made the hash in the manifest, so the two values can be compared directly.

practice.q: Where does the run's gateway token come from?

options.text: It is written onto the VM at claim time and dies with the run
options.why: Anything per run is written at claim time, never baked.

options.text: It is baked into the image and rotated nightly
options.why: A baked token would be shared by every VM from that image, and readable by any of them.

options.text: The harness downloads it from the internet
options.why: The VM has no road out, and tokens never come from outside our services.

practice.q: Put the night and the next morning in order.
items: The nightly job bakes the image and writes the manifest
A smoke test boots one VM from it and runs one end-to-end test
The image's ID is written to the parameter the launch templates read
A run claims a VM and freshen compares lockfile hashes with the manifest
Only the installs whose lockfile changed run again
practice.why: Bake, prove, promote, then do only the difference at claim time.

practice.q: freshen fetches the run's commit, but the checkout still shows last night's main. What is the likely cause?

options.text: origin still points at the baked mirror instead of the broker
options.why: A clone made with --reference keeps the mirror as origin, so freshen must point origin at the broker before fetching.

options.text: The manifest has the wrong lockfile hash
options.why: The manifest only decides installs. Which commits git can see depends on where it fetches from.
Git fetches by commit, not by time.
